headline: Iron ore sinks to its lowest since September 2024
detail: Singapore iron ore futures touched $89.25 a ton Tuesday as Chinese mills buy only what they need heading into the slow winter season and big miners ship more. One analyst sees $85–86 in November, which keeps pressure on steel and ferrous scrap.

headline: Copper climbs to its best close in about two weeks
detail: LME three-month copper rose 1.1% to about $14,488 a ton and COMEX copper had its highest close since Oct. 14, near $6.63 a pound, on renewed AI buying and tight supply. Firmer copper should support bare bright and #1 bids.

headline: Fed decision today; hold expected, December hike odds above 80%
detail: The Fed announces at 1pm Central. Futures price about an 84% chance of a December rate hike after an attack on a Saudi refinery pushed oil back up, and a hawkish tone would lift the dollar and weigh on metals.

headline: Teck's Highland Valley mine runs at reduced capacity during strike
detail: More than 1,200 Steelworkers walked out Oct. 24 at Canada's biggest copper mine over pay, pensions and staffing, and Teck says output is reduced. A long strike tightens North American copper supply.

headline: Nucor lifts spot hot-rolled coil to $1,270 a ton
detail: Nucor raised its weekly spot HRC price $15 to $1,270 per short ton, its 14th straight weekly increase, with lead times of three to five weeks. Strong mill pricing supports demand for prime and shredded scrap.

headline: Nucor: scrap costs flat, fourth quarter steady
detail: Nucor earned $5.80 a share in Q3 and paid an average $421 per gross ton for scrap and substitutes, about the same as Q2. It sees Q4 earnings flat to slightly higher, a sign the biggest US scrap buyer expects steady mill demand.

headline: Mills expected to pay more for ferrous scrap in November
detail: Market players surveyed by Steel Market Update expect November ferrous scrap prices to rise. Firm steel prices and steady mill runs back that up, though iron ore's slide is a risk.

headline: US and Canada work on a deal to ease steel and auto tariffs
detail: Sources say the two countries are negotiating lower tariffs on Canadian steel, aluminum and autos ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms. Lower tariffs could bring more Canadian metal south and soften US premiums.

headline: China's copper import premium hits a near 13-year high
detail: The Yangshan premium reached $188 a ton and Shanghai exchange copper stocks fell more than 25% last week as smelters went into maintenance. Strong Chinese buying keeps global copper tight.

headline: Aluminum hits a four-week high on thin LME stocks
detail: LME aluminum rose to about $3,105 a ton early Wednesday after orders to pull 3,500 tons from Asian warehouses; most metal left on warrant is Russian, which many buyers avoid. Tighter supply supports aluminum scrap bids.

headline: China's copper scrap imports jump 33% in September
detail: China imported about 237,000 tons of copper scrap in September, up 33% from August, as its import window opened; US shipments are recovering from a very low base. Strong Chinese demand helps support copper scrap prices.

headline: Stellantis: North American shipments down 12% in Q3
detail: Stellantis said North American shipments fell to 357,000 after a planned Grand Cherokee and Compass shutdown, and it expects about €1 billion in tariff costs this year. It kept its full-year outlook and expects more shipments in Q4, which means more auto scrap and steel demand.

headline: New home sales slip to a 676,000 pace in September
detail: Sales of new homes dipped 0.6% from August and are down 5% from a year ago, though they beat forecasts; supply sits at 8.4 months. Slow housing means less demand for copper wire, plumbing and building steel.

headline: Consumer confidence jumps to its best since June
detail: The Conference Board index rose 7.5 points to 91.7 in October as gas prices eased, the first gain in four months. Stronger consumers help car and appliance demand but can also push the Fed toward a hike.

headline: Durable goods orders rise 1.8% in September
detail: Orders for long-lasting goods beat forecasts, mostly on aircraft; excluding transportation they rose 0.5%. Steady factory orders support steel, copper and aluminum use.

headline: Gold gains 1% Tuesday, slips Wednesday as oil jumps
detail: Gold rose about 1% to roughly $4,058 Tuesday as oil eased, then dipped to about $4,045 early Wednesday after a refinery attack revived inflation worries. Silver followed, near $54.

headline: Fund traders cut gold bets ahead of the Fed
detail: SP Angel says trend-following funds have trimmed gold positions and some have gone short, with gold ETF holdings slipping. Fund selling can make gold and silver swing harder after the Fed.

headline: Analysts cut platinum and palladium forecasts again
detail: A Reuters survey shows analysts lowered their 2026 platinum and palladium price outlooks for a third straight quarter, citing high rates and a strong dollar. That points to softer catalytic converter values.

headline: Nornickel nickel output up 41%, smelter overhaul planned
detail: Nornickel's Q3 nickel output rose 41% from Q2 to 61,000 tons, but it will overhaul a smelter for nine months next year, which may cut 2027 supply. More supply now keeps nickel and stainless scrap prices soft.

headline: Congo arrests in copper belt raise supply worries
detail: Congo suspended the head of its small-scale mining agency after about 300 Chinese nationals were detained in the Kolwezi copper belt. Trouble in Congo can disrupt copper and cobalt supply.

headline: Copper miners rally; odds of a copper cable tariff near 25%
detail: Southern Copper jumped 4.5% and Freeport 1.2% Tuesday. Prediction markets give about a 25% chance of US tariffs on insulated copper cable by year-end, which would affect wire scrap flows.

headline: China factory profits rise 14.4% in September
detail: Chinese industrial profits grew at the fastest pace since June, led by AI-related and mining sectors, while consumer industries lagged. Better profits help metals demand but lower the odds of new stimulus.

headline: Converter buyers still average about $90 a unit
detail: RRCats' national average held near $90 a converter on Oct. 26, with large foreign cats at $90–$450 and regular domestic at $20–$128. Expect softer bids if platinum's overnight drop holds.

headline: Indonesia cuts its nickel benchmark price 2.9%
detail: Indonesia lowered its late-October nickel reference price by $475 to about $15,848 a ton as new mining quotas push ore prices down. LME nickel's official price slipped 1% to $15,535; cheaper nickel weighs on stainless scrap.

headline: Stellantis Canada workers authorize a strike
detail: Unifor members voted 97.3% for a strike mandate covering more than 9,000 Stellantis workers; Windsor Assembly would be hit first. A strike would cut Canadian vehicle output and steel demand.

headline: Housing starts fall 5.2% in September
detail: Starts dropped to a 1.22 million annual pace and single-family permits fell 4%. New-home sales come out Tuesday morning for another read on construction demand.

headline: US-Mexico trade deal stalls over 50% steel tariffs
detail: Talks with Mexico have stalled on how much to cut US steel and aluminum tariffs, and may wait until after the midterms. High tariffs keep US steel prices, and scrap demand, elevated.

headline: World steel output dips 0.2% in September; US up 4.3%
detail: Global crude steel output was 142.4 million tons in September; China was flat at 73.6 million and the US rose 4.3% to 7.2 million. Higher US output means steady demand for scrap from EAF mills.
